title: Tensor tiling IO priority and runtime safety
content:
Overview:

This doc proposes a tile-based parameter residency model for the serving runtime that is focused on three combined goals: lower cold-start IO, predictable latency under bursty traffic, and safe atomic activation for hot-swapping/rollouts. The idea is to split large tensors (embeddings, attention, MLP kernels, layernorm scalars) into small, independently addressable tiles that the runtime can page in/out, prefetch, and activate with fine-grained priority control.

Why tiling vs coarse weight pages:
- Fine-grained (64KB–1MB) tiles reduce wasted IO when only a small slice of a large kernel is needed for short sequences or for models with block-sparse ops.
- Smaller residency units enable smarter eviction that respects KV cache locality and request hot paths.
- Enables partial activation: we can bring compute-critical tiles online first (attention weights, rotary params), leaving less-critical tiles (output projection, non-causal MLP branches) lazy.

Key concepts and components:

1) Tile: smallest IO/residency unit. Identified by (model-id, weight-path, tile-index, version-id).
2) TileState: {UNMAPPED, MAPPED_READ, MAPPED_WRITE, PENDING_ACTIVATION, ACTIVE, EVICTED} (note: this is conceptual — implementation flags are bitmasks).
3) ResidencyMap: in-memory structure mapping model -> tile ranges to residency/age counters and priority buckets. Lightweight; stored in sharded slices for lock contention reduction.
4) IO priority lanes: three lanes — realtime, background-prefetch, lazy-on-demand. Each lane maps to different kernel thread pools and OS-level QoS where supported (blkio cgroups, io_uring priority, NIC QoS for remote fetch).

Tile sizing guidance (empirical):
- Default tile size: 256KB for fp16/fp32 checkpoints stored as safetensors; quantized shards can use smaller tiles (64KB) because disk bandwidth is lower cost than extra metadata overhead.
- Tunable via model manifest: models from repository should include tile_hint and critical_tile_ranges.

Loading strategy (high-level flow):
1) On model load request, consult model manifest for tile map and critical ranges.
2) Immediately map index/manifest (safe memory-mapped small file).
3) Issue asynchronous real-time reads for critical tiles in realtime lane; fallback to dedicated DMA threads for GPUs with direct BDMA support.
4) Start background-prefetch for mid-priority tiles predicted by the sequence length distribution and KV cache index.
5) Lazy-on-demand for everything else; requests hitting missing tiles trigger an on-demand fetch with a short spin/wait window (configurable ms) intended to batch across concurrent requests.

KV cache interplay and affinity:
- Each active conversation keeps a light affinity map: preferred tiles for the conversation based on previously accessed layers/time-decay. Affinity scores bias prefetch and eviction decisions so that hot conversations experience fewer misses.
- When a KV cache entry references a tile that has been evicted, the planner will escalate prefetch priority for that tile to realtime for that conversation (soft pin). This avoids cascading misses for long-context retrieval.

Prefetch heuristics (proposal):
- Layer-based: always prefetch attention QKV tiles one layer ahead of execution when sequence length indicates reuse.
- Sequence-length aware: for short generations (<64 tokens) avoid prefetching large MLP output tiles beyond the active depth.
- Stochastic early fetch: sample 1–2 tiles from deeper layers to reduce tail latency on unexpectedly long requests — controlled by per-model sampling rate.

Atomic activation and safety for hot-swap/rollouts:
- Tiles carry a version-id. New model rollout stages upload tile sets with a staged commit manifest that includes checksums (SHA256) and an activation plan.
- Activation is two-phase: stage-in (fetch tiles into MAPPED_READ, validate checksums) then commit (flip version pointer atomically for the model handle).
- Active runtime threads reference a model handle that is immutable; swap is done by CAS on the handle pointer to avoid tearing. Long-held operations increment a per-handle refcount so eviction of older handles waits for in-flight requests to drain or be rerouted.
- Fallback policy: if commit fails mid-activation, we keep serving the prior handle and mark the new tiled set as failed for rollback and debugging. All failures log a diagnostic bundle with tile checksums and fetch traces.

Memory-mapped vs read-into-buffer tradeoffs:
- Use mmap for index files, manifests, and small tiles when underlying FS supports sparse mmap and page-locking (helps zero-copy on some kernels). mmap creates easier eviction semantics and small resident set accounting.
- For large tiles or when GPU DMA paths expect contiguous pinned memory, adopt read-into-pinned buffers and register the buffer with the device. The runtime should be able to transparently convert a tile from mmap to pinned buffer on first-use by a GPU operation.

Safetensors storage notes:
- Store tiles as standalone safetensors shards with metadata header that includes tile-index, layer, dtype, and checksum. This keeps shard discovery simple and compatible with existing safetensors toolchains.
- Provide a "tile manifest" jsonl file for each model version mapping tensors -> shard files with byte offsets. This allows single-file safetensors with internal tiling for legacy exporters.

Eviction policy (hybrid):
- Age + affinity + cost. Score(tile) = alpha*recency + beta*affinity + gamma*fetch-cost. Tune weights per workload.
- Special-case pinned tiles: some tiles can be pinned by policy (security-critical or low-latency wheels) and are only evicted under memory pressure above a threshold.

IO scheduling internals (implementation notes):
- Abstract IO as lane-based work items. Each lane has a limited concurrency and separate queues to avoid head-of-line blocking. Use io_uring for batching where available, with a dedicated submission ring per lane to segregate priorities.
- Implement an adaptive backoff/batching window for on-demand fetches: short-window (1–3ms) to coalesce concurrent misses for the same tile across threads. Window length is dynamic based on current QPS and latency SLO.

Safety and observability hooks:
- Emit events for: tile_miss, tile_prefetch_hit, tile_evicted, tile_activated, activation_failed. Keep these per-request as trace tags so root cause is visible in distributed traces.
- Expose residency heatmap per model via Console for operators (tile-level residency rate, fetch latency distribution).

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- Optimal default tile size for quantized int8 shards across different filesystems (ext4, xfs, networked blobstore) — we need empirical benchmarks on CI nodes with representative disks.
- OS-level QoS portability: mapping runtime lanes to blkio cgroup v2 vs io_uring priorities is OS-specific. Define a pluggable adapter and fallbacks.
- Metadata overhead tradeoff: very small tiles increase manifest size and RPC overhead. Consider a two-level index (tile-run-length encoding) for repeated contiguous tiles.

Implementation checklist (MVP):
- [ ] Tile manifest format + exporter test harness for safetensors shards.
- [ ] ResidencyMap prototype + basic eviction scoring (recency only).
- [ ] IO lane abstraction + io_uring-backed realtime lane for Linux (fallback threadpool for others).
- [ ] Atomic activation flow: staged fetch -> checksum validation -> handle swap with refcounts.
- [ ] KV cache affinity proof-of-concept and simple tie-in to prefetcher.
- [ ] Basic metrics/events: tile_miss, fetch_latency_ms, residency_pct per-layer.

Notes to implementer (practical tips):
- Start with a userspace in-memory ResidencyMap and implement tiled fetch via local files before adding remote blobstore adapters — easier to iterate.
- Keep tile metadata compact and memory-resident; avoid per-tile heavy locking by sharding the map and using lock-free counters where possible.
- Build a fuzz test that simulates rollouts plus concurrent long-running inferences to validate atomic activation behaviour.

Slack threads and references: #serving-runtime/tensor-tiling (design notes), PR draft linked above.

Quick sketch of tile manifest line (jsonl):
{"tensor": "encoder/layer_3/attn/q/kernel", "shard": "q_0001.safetensors", "offset": 131072, "length": 262144, "tile_index": 3, "checksum": "sha256:...", "critical": true}

End of doc.
